United States: The United States has thousands of universities, and most international funding comes from the universities themselves: merit scholarships, need-based aid at top colleges, and graduate assistantships that pay tuition and a stipend for master's and PhD students. Government programmes such as Fulbright are available in many countries. Many US universities also offer application fee waivers.
United Kingdom: In the United Kingdom, major funding comes from government programmes such as Chevening and the Commonwealth Scholarships, plus university awards and funded PhD studentships from research councils. Master's degrees usually last one year, which makes UK scholarships good value.
Canada: Canada offers entrance scholarships at universities such as Toronto, McGill and UBC, funded graduate programmes, and provincial awards. Many funded master's and PhD programmes pay a stipend through teaching or research assistantships.
Germany: Germany is popular because most public universities charge little or no tuition. Funding comes mainly from DAAD scholarships, the Deutschlandstipendium and Germany's political and church-backed foundations. Many PhD positions are paid jobs with a salary.
France: France's flagship award is the Eiffel Excellence Scholarship for master's and PhD students. Universities such as Sciences Po and many grandes écoles also offer their own scholarships. Tuition at public universities is relatively low.
Italy: Italy offers regional need-based scholarships (such as EDiSU and DSU awards) that can include free accommodation, meals and a yearly grant, plus merit scholarships at universities like Politecnico di Milano and Italian government scholarships.
Netherlands: In the Netherlands, international students can apply for university excellence scholarships, the NL Scholarship and funded PhD positions, which are usually paid jobs. Many master's programmes are taught in English.
Japan: Japan's main award is the MEXT Japanese Government Scholarship, which covers tuition, a monthly allowance and flights. Universities and private foundations also offer scholarships, and many graduate programmes are taught in English.
South Korea: South Korea offers the Global Korea Scholarship (GKS), funded by the government, and generous university scholarships at institutions such as KAIST and Yeungnam. Many awards cover tuition and a monthly stipend.
China: China's main funding is the Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC), which covers tuition, accommodation, a stipend and insurance. Many universities also offer their own scholarships, and a growing number of programmes are taught in English.
Türkiye: Türkiye offers the government's Türkiye Burslari scholarship for all levels, plus scholarships at private universities such as Sabancı. Many programmes are taught in English.
Hungary: Hungary's Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship covers tuition, a monthly allowance, accommodation and insurance for students from partner countries, at bachelor's, master's and PhD level.
Australia: Australia's universities offer research training scholarships for master's by research and PhD students, which cover tuition and a living stipend, as well as merit scholarships for coursework degrees.
Nigeria: These opportunities are for study or programmes in Nigeria, including state and federal government scholarships, university awards and private foundation scholarships for Nigerian students.
Qatar: Qatar's universities, including Hamad Bin Khalifa University and Doha Institute for Graduate Studies, offer scholarships that can cover tuition, accommodation and a monthly stipend.
Saudi Arabia: Saudi universities such as KAUST and Qassim University offer fully funded scholarships to international students, often including tuition, housing, a stipend and flights.
Hong Kong: Hong Kong's main award for doctoral students is the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme, which pays one of the highest PhD stipends in the world, plus university scholarships for master's students.
Taiwan: Taiwan offers the Ministry of Education's Taiwan Scholarship, which pays tuition and a monthly stipend, and university scholarships at institutions across the island.
Sweden: Sweden's main award is the Swedish Institute Scholarship, plus university tuition waivers for non-EU students. Most master's programmes are taught in English.
Denmark: Denmark's universities award Danish Government Scholarships to top non-EU master's students, covering a tuition waiver and, in many faculties, a living grant.
Switzerland: Swiss universities such as ETH Zurich, EPFL and the University of Lausanne offer master's scholarships for international students, and many PhD positions are paid.
Ghana: Ghana's universities host DAAD In-Country/In-Region scholarships and Mastercard Foundation programmes that fully fund master's study for African students.
